successors.note: Merged into Ayutthaya in 1351; the page ends the kingdom in 1438, when it was 'completely annexed'. The ayutthaya-kingdom dossier already includes Suphan Buri in its 1351 founding region.

capitals.name: Suphanburi (Songphanuri)
capitals.note: The text places the seat at Suphan Buri and at Phanthumburi/Devanagara; the page gives no dated moves.

correction.text: the Tha Chin valley: the page says the kingdom 'straddled the Tha Chin River in a north-south direction' (Suphan Buri, Nakhon Pathom, Chai Nat, Samut Sakhon)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row): infobox '913 - 1438'; the text puts the founding in 877 and the freedom of Suphannabhum in 913, 'after its suzerain, Nakhon Pathom of Kamalanka, fell to Phetchaburi in 913'. The page also says it 'stretched across Siam proper from west-central Thailand to north of the Kra Isthmus'; only the Tha Chin valley is drawn because the page names no other place. Infobox area: none (moat 1900 x 3600 m).

correction.text: the Tha Chin valley: the page says the kingdom 'straddled the Tha Chin River in a north-south direction' (Suphan Buri, Nakhon Pathom, Chai Nat, Samut Sakhon)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the same core after leaving Sukhothai. 'After Ram Khamhaeng died in 1298, its vassals began to break away.' The Chinese records call it Xian 'since 1349'. 1283-1299 is left to Sukhothai (see the ledger).

region.text: the Tha Chin valley: the page says the kingdom 'straddled the Tha Chin River in a north-south direction' (Suphan Buri, Nakhon Pathom, Chai Nat, Samut Sakhon)

ledger.note: 913: Suphannabhum becomes free. The page says it was founded in 877 and became free 'after its suzerain, Nakhon Pathom of Kamalanka, fell to Phetchaburi in 913'; the infobox reads 913-1438. Its Uthong ancestry runs to the ancient port of Mueang Uthong, 'the center of the Dvaravati civilization' for Coedes.

region.text: the Tha Chin valley: the page says the kingdom 'straddled the Tha Chin River in a north-south direction' (Suphan Buri, Nakhon Pathom, Chai Nat, Samut Sakhon)

ledger.note: 1283: Sukhothai takes Suphannabhum. The page says it was a tributary of Sukhothai and 'annexed to the Sukhothai Kingdom in 1283'. The Ayutthaya Kingdom page names only Phrip Phri and Nakhon Si Thammarat as Sukhothai tributaries 'between about 1283 and 1298', so the claim rests on one page.

region.text: the Tha Chin valley: the page says the kingdom 'straddled the Tha Chin River in a north-south direction' (Suphan Buri, Nakhon Pathom, Chai Nat, Samut Sakhon)

ledger.note: c. 1300: Suphannabhum breaks away from Sukhothai. The page says only that 'After Ram Khamhaeng died in 1298, its vassals began to break away'; the year 1300 is bridged from the sukhothai-kingdom dossier's loss ('Suphannaphum Kingdom ... left early in Loe Thai's reign').

region.text: the Tha Chin valley: the page says the kingdom 'straddled the Tha Chin River in a north-south direction' (Suphan Buri, Nakhon Pathom, Chai Nat, Samut Sakhon)

ledger.note: 1351: Suphanburi joins Lopburi, Ayodhya and Phetchaburi in the new Ayutthaya Kingdom. 'Ayutthaya emerged from the merger of four port polities of the lower basin' (Lopburi, Suphanburi, Ayodhya, Phetchaburi) and '4 March 1351 is conventionally given as the foundation'; U Thong V, who had ruled Suphanburi from 1341, 'added Suphannabhum and Lavo through marriage' (Suphannabhum page). The union 'was not as clean as the date suggests'.

region.text: the Tha Chin valley: the page says the kingdom 'straddled the Tha Chin River in a north-south direction' (Suphan Buri, Nakhon Pathom, Chai Nat, Samut Sakhon)

ledger.note: 1351: the Suphannabhum kingdom is absorbed into Ayutthaya. U Thong V was enthroned 'by uniting all principalities in the lower Menam Valley in 1350/1351' and sent Borommarachathirat I to rule Suphanburi; the Suphannabhum line took the Ayutthaya throne in 1370 and 1408, and the infobox ends the kingdom in 1438, 'completely annexed to Ayutthaya'.

certainty.note: The page names a river and a moat, not a frontier.

sources.title: Ayutthaya Kingdom
sources.note: The 1351 merger of Lopburi, Suphanburi, Ayodhya and Phetchaburi; the Sukhothai tributaries; the Suphannabhum line on the throne.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks; named by se-01-b and se-01-d (Sukhothai's loss c. 1300) as needing a dossier. Two pages opened. Not settled: (1) the page's dates are inconsistent (founded 877, free 913, 'Uthong I took it in 1163' on the Ayutthaya page, infobox 913-1438): 913 and 1351 are used for the independent state, and 1351-1438 as part of Ayutthaya ruled by crown princes; (2) the 1283 annexation by Sukhothai is on the Suphannabhum page only, and the Ayutthaya page lists only Phrip Phri and Nakhon Si Thammarat as Sukhothai's tributaries; sukhothai-kingdom carries the same land under a 1294-1300 gain without a 1283 date; (3) the extent is the Tha Chin valley, although the page says the kingdom stretched 'to north of the Kra Isthmus'; (4) Phrip Phli (Phetchaburi), which conquered Nakhon Pathom in 913 on this page and joined Ayutthaya in 1351, needs its own dossier (suggested slug phip-phli) if the orchestrator wants it; Lavo/Lopburi seized Suphannabhum at an undated time (infobox 'Lavo seized Suphannabhum').
